foundation_quote.quote: Academic requirements: Successful completion of Attestat/Certificate of Secondary Education with grade average of 4

gpa.how_found: Kazakhstan country page (tcd.ie/study/country/kazakhstan/) found by site search; cross-checked Table 1 (Overall Competitive Admission Bands) of the 2027 Undergraduate Admission Guide for non-EU Students PDF.
gpa.notes: No published direct-entry grade threshold exists for the Kazakhstan Attestat or the NIS Grade 12 certificate: Kazakhstan does not appear in Table 1 of the non-EU Admission Guide (Russia Attestat does, avg 4.9-5.0), and the country page lists only A Levels, IB, or US HS Diploma with SAT/ACT for direct application. The only published threshold for the Kazakh certificate (grade average of 4) is for the Trinity International Foundation Programme, not the degree. NIS is not named on any page read; applicant should confirm with study@tcd.ie whether the NIS Grade 12 certificate is accepted. For direct entry via A Level/IB/SAT, Computer Science requires Mathematics at subject level 2 and overall admission band 3 (guide Table 4); course page: A-Level Grade C Mathematics, IB HL Grade 5 Mathematics. Admission is competitive: 'posted scores are minimum entrance requirements only and do not guarantee admission.'

deadline.quote: As this programme is reaching full capacity we are closing direct applications for Non EU/International applicants on Friday 1 May 2026.
deadline.how_found: Course page Overview banner and Non-EU apply link date (01/MAY/2026); cross-checked against the Direct Applications page 'Application Dates' table.
deadline.notes: Only the 2026-entry cycle is published (applications opened 1 November 2025). No September 2027 deadline is published yet as of 2026-10-17. For 2026 entry Computer Science closed early (1 May 2026) because it reached capacity; the general non-EU closing date was 30 June 2026, with 1 February as priority deadline (How to Apply page: 'February 1st is Priority Deadline* to receive a decision by April 1st'). Expect the 2027 cycle to open around 1 November 2026; apply early as CS may fill before 30 June.

scholarship_exists.how_found: Site search for Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship; that page excludes computer science and links ('see here') to the E3 scholarships page, which lists B.A. Computer Science as an eligible major.
scholarship_exists.notes: The general Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship (€2,000-€5,000) does NOT apply: 'Medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt from this scholarship programme.' E3 page currently shows 2026 batch deadlines (1 Feb, 15 Mar, 1 May 2026, then rolling); 2027 dates not yet published. Partial award (tuition reduction), not full funding.
